faq.5.q: How do I know whether my AC needs gas filling?
faq.5.a: Weak cooling, ice on the copper pipes or a hissing sound can point to low gas, but dirty filters and electrical faults cause similar symptoms. A technician needs to inspect the AC to confirm.

faq.14.q: How often should an AC be serviced?
faq.14.a: In a hot place like Narasaraopet, most homes service their AC before summer and once more during heavy use. ACs that run many hours a day or sit near dusty roads may need cleaning more often.
faq.15.q: Why is water leaking from my AC?
faq.15.a: Water leakage from the indoor unit is usually caused by a blocked drain pipe, an incorrect drain slope, or ice forming on the coil because of dirty filters or low refrigerant. A technician can find the exact cause and clear it.
faq.16.q: Is AC gas filling needed every year?
faq.16.a: No. An AC works in a sealed circuit, so the gas is not used up in normal running. If your AC needs gas every year, there is a leak that should be found and repaired before refilling.
faq.17.q: What should I check before calling an AC technician?
faq.17.a: Check that the power supply and MCB are on, the remote has working batteries and is set to Cool mode, and the filters are not heavily clogged. If the AC still does not cool, switch it off and call a technician rather than running it for hours.

This website is run by BOBBY AC REPAIR & HOME APPLIANCE SERVICES, Narasaraopet, Andhra Pradesh. We respect your privacy and collect as little information as possible.

What we collect

The website does not have user accounts and does not store your booking details on a server. When you use the booking form, your details are placed into a WhatsApp message on your own device. Nothing is sent until you choose to send it.

How we use your details

Information you send by phone or WhatsApp (such as your name, number, area and appliance problem) is used only to arrange and carry out your service. We do not sell or share it for marketing.

Third-party services

The site loads a map from Google Maps (fonts are served from this website itself). Google Maps may receive basic technical information such as your IP address. WhatsApp is governed by its own privacy policy.

The website is hosted on Cloudflare Pages, which processes basic request information (such as your IP address) to deliver pages securely. Product photos on the AC Spare Parts page load from ApnaSpare (apnaspare.com). The site does not use advertising or analytics cookies.

Your language choice

Location

Contact

sp.id.h: How to Identify the Correct AC Spare Part
sp.id.sub: Most wrong-part problems come from guessing. These steps help us match the exact part the first time.
sp.id.1.d: The sticker on the side of the indoor unit and on the outdoor unit shows the brand, model number, capacity, refrigerant (R32, R410A or R22) and voltage.
sp.id.2.d: Inverter ACs use different PCBs, compressors and fan motors. A non-inverter part will not work in an inverter unit, and the reverse.
sp.id.3.d: Capacitors show MFD and voltage, motors show wattage and rotation, PCBs carry a part code. Matching these values matters more than the brand name.
sp.id.4.d: Take photos of the part, its label and its wiring from two angles. This avoids wiring mistakes when the new part is fitted.
sp.id.5.d: Symptoms often overlap — a dead outdoor unit can be a capacitor, contactor, PCB or wiring fault. Replacing a part without testing wastes money.
sp.safe: AC units carry mains voltage, and capacitors can hold a charge even after the power is switched off. Compressor, coil, valve and gas work involves pressurised refrigerant and brazing. Please do not open the AC or attempt these replacements yourself — have a trained technician do it.

sp.faq.3.q: Why is a price shown as a range?
sp.faq.3.a: The same part differs by brand, model, tonnage, rating, and whether it is genuine or compatible. Different sellers also price differently, so a range is more honest than a single number.
sp.faq.4.q: Is PCB repair the same as a new PCB?
sp.faq.4.a: No. PCB repair fixes your existing board at component level and usually costs less. A new original board is model-specific and priced on request. A universal PCB kit is a cheaper alternative but changes the remote and some features.

sp.faq.6.q: Will a universal or compatible part fit my AC?

sp.faq.9.q: How long does a part replacement take?

asm.in1.d: The rear chassis carries every internal part and hooks onto the wall-mounting plate.
asm.in2.d: Copper tubes with aluminium fins. Cold refrigerant evaporates inside and absorbs heat from the room air.
asm.in3.d: A long tangential wheel that pulls room air through the coil and spreads it evenly.
asm.in4.d: Drives the blower at Low, Medium, High or Auto speed.
asm.in5.d: Mesh filters trap dust before it reaches the coil. Clean them every 2–4 weeks.
asm.in6.d: Sits under the coil and collects the water condensed out of humid air.
asm.in7.d: Carries the condensate out of the room on a continuous downward slope.
asm.in8.d: Thermistors read the room and coil temperature so the AC knows when to cool, slow down or stop.
asm.in9.d: The indoor brain: reads the remote and sensors, runs the fan, louver and display, and talks to the outdoor unit.
asm.in10.d: Shows the set temperature and mode, and holds the remote's infrared receiver.
asm.in11.d: A small stepper motor swings the louver to aim the cool air up, down or across the room.
asm.in12.d: Closes the unit over the filters and lifts open for cleaning.
asm.out1.d: Weather-resistant steel base and frame; a partition separates the fan side from the compressor side.
asm.out2.d: The heart of the system: it compresses refrigerant gas, raising its pressure and temperature.
asm.out3.d: Hot refrigerant releases your room's heat to the outside air here and condenses back to liquid.
asm.out4.d: Pulls outside air through the condenser coil to carry the heat away.
asm.out5.d: Drives the propeller fan from a bracket in the fan compartment.
asm.out6.d: Controls the compressor and fan; in inverter models it also varies the compressor speed.
asm.out7.d: Helps start and run the compressor and fan motors, mainly in non-inverter models.
asm.out8.d: Brass valves where the copper pipes connect; used for vacuuming, gas charging and isolation.
asm.out9.d: Where the interconnect cable from the indoor unit and the power supply are terminated.
asm.out10.d: Guards the fan blades while letting air flow freely.
asm.ins1.d: Fixed level on a solid wall, with clearance above and at the sides.
asm.ins2.d: A hole of about 65 mm, drilled sloping slightly down to the outside and lined with a sleeve.
asm.ins3.d: Mounted level on rated brackets with room for airflow and service, on anti-vibration pads.
asm.ins4.d: Two insulated copper lines — liquid and gas — flared and tightened onto the service valves.
asm.ins5.d: The interconnect cable runs to the outdoor terminal block on a dedicated, properly earthed supply.
asm.ins6.d: Routed with a continuous downward slope to a safe drain point, never upward.
asm.ins7.d: Lines are vacuumed and leak-tested before the valves open; the wall hole is sealed and pipes taped neatly.

sys1.d: Hangs on the wall inside the room. It pulls in warm room air, cools it over the evaporator coil and blows it back.
sys1.u: It holds the filters, coil, blower and controls — the parts cleaned during routine servicing.
sys2.d: Sits outside. The compressor and condenser release the heat taken out of your room.
sys2.u: It needs open space around it so the hot air can escape.
sys3.d: Two insulated copper lines carry refrigerant between the units in a closed loop.
sys3.u: Leaks at the joints are the main reason an AC needs gas refilling.
sys4.d: The interconnect cable carries power and control signals between the units.
sys4.u: The AC needs a dedicated, properly earthed supply.
sys5.d: Carries the water removed from the air out of the room.
sys5.u: It must slope downward all the way, or water drips indoors.
cool1.d: The indoor fan pulls warm air in through the top grille.
cool2.d: Mesh filters trap dust before the air reaches the coil.
cool3: Air passes the cold evaporator coil
cool3.d: Refrigerant inside the coil evaporates and absorbs heat, so the air leaving the coil is cooler and drier.
cool4: The blower sends cool air into the room
cool4.d: The cross-flow blower and louver spread cool air evenly across the room.
cool5.d: The compressor draws the refrigerant, now carrying the room's heat, to the outdoor unit and compresses it.
cool6.d: The outdoor fan blows air across the condenser coil and the heat leaves with the warm air. The cooled refrigerant then returns indoors.
asm.in12.u: Lift it to reach the filters — that is how you clean them at home.
asm.in5.u: Clogged filters cut airflow and raise power use; cleaning them is the easiest maintenance.
asm.in2.u: Dust on the coil reduces cooling and causes bad smells; it is cleaned during AC servicing.
asm.in3.u: Dust build-up on the blades makes the airflow weak and noisy.
asm.in4.u: If the indoor fan does not run, the room will not cool even when the outdoor unit works.
asm.in6.u: A blocked pan or drain is the usual reason for water dripping from the indoor unit.
asm.in7.u: A sag or kink in the hose causes water leakage.
asm.in8.u: A faulty sensor can make the AC stop too early or run without stopping.
asm.in9.u: Power surges and moisture can damage it; error codes on the display often point here.

Why Does an AC Stop Cooling During Summer? Causes, Checks & Fixes
Your AC cooled fine in March but struggles in May? Here is why peak summer exposes weak parts, what you can check safely, and what needs a technician.

Quick answer: an AC usually stops cooling in peak summer because the outdoor unit cannot throw heat out fast enough. A dusty condenser coil, a weak capacitor, low refrigerant from a slow leak, low voltage, or an AC that is too small for the room all show up first when it is 42–45°C outside. Clean filters and give the outdoor unit open air first; if cooling is still weak, get the AC inspected before the compressor overheats.

Many Narasaraopet homes notice the same pattern every year: the AC is comfortable in March, but by late April and May the room never gets properly cold, the outdoor unit runs non-stop, and the electricity bill jumps. That is not bad luck. Heat removal gets much harder as the outside temperature climbs, and any small weakness that went unnoticed in mild weather is suddenly exposed.

Why summer is the real test for an AC

An AC does not "make cold". It moves heat from your room to the outdoor unit, and the outdoor condenser coil releases that heat into outside air. The hotter that outside air is, the harder the condenser has to work. India's BEE star rating uses the ISEER method precisely because Indian ACs must keep working across a wide range of outdoor temperatures, up to the mid-40s. In Palnadu district, IMD heatwave warnings in April and May often mean outdoor units sit in direct sun at 45°C or more.

So the AC has less "spare capacity" in summer. A coil that is 20% blocked with dust, or a capacitor that has lost some strength, may be fine at 32°C but fail to keep up at 44°C.

7 common reasons an AC stops cooling in summer

1. Dirty condenser coil or blocked outdoor unit

Dust, leaves, bird nests or a wall placed too close in front of the outdoor unit trap hot air. The unit keeps recycling its own hot exhaust. Look for a unit that is very hot to touch and blowing weak, hot air. A proper outdoor unit cleaning often restores cooling in one visit.

2. Clogged indoor filters and coil

If the indoor filter is choked, less room air passes over the cold coil. The coil can even freeze, and then airflow drops further. Filters should be washed every 2 weeks in summer.

3. Weak or failed capacitor

The capacitor helps the compressor and fan motor start. Heat ages capacitors quickly. A weak one may let the fan spin but the compressor struggle or click on and off. It is a common, inexpensive part; see indicative prices on our AC spare parts price list.

4. Low refrigerant because of a leak

Gas does not "get used up". If it is low, it has leaked from a joint or coil. Symptoms include ice on the copper pipes, hissing, or cooling that gets slowly worse. The fix is to find and repair the leak first, then charge the correct amount; read AC gas filling cost: R32 vs R410A.

5. Low or fluctuating voltage

Summer evenings bring peak power demand. Low voltage makes the compressor draw more current and overheat, and protection may cut it out. A suitable stabiliser (for non-inverter ACs) and healthy wiring help.

6. AC too small for the room or heat load

A top-floor bedroom with a sun-facing wall, or a room with many people, may simply need more capacity than a 1-ton AC can give at 44°C.

7. Wrong settings

Eco, sleep or Dry mode, a very low fan speed, or a timer can all limit cooling. Since BEE rules, new star-labelled ACs default to 24°C, which is efficient but may feel warm in a hot room until it settles.

Safe checks you can do before calling

CheckWhat to look for
Mode and settingCool mode, 24–26°C, fan on Auto or High
Indoor filtersWash with plain water, dry fully, refit
Outdoor unitAt least 1–2 feet of open space in front; nothing covering it
Doors and windowsClosed; curtains drawn on sun-facing glass
Ice on pipesIf you see ice, switch off and call: do not keep running

Do not open electrical covers, touch capacitors (they can hold a charge) or try to add gas yourself.

When to call a technician

  • The outdoor unit fan runs but air indoors is not cold.
  • The outdoor unit hums, clicks or keeps switching on and off.
  • Ice forms on the pipes or the indoor coil.
  • The MCB trips or there is a burning smell (switch off immediately).
  • Cooling stays weak after cleaning filters and clearing the outdoor unit.

BOBBY inspects the AC first, explains the fault and gives you an estimate before any repair. You can also check a quick estimate online or book AC repair in Narasaraopet.

Inverter vs non-inverter ACs in extreme heat

Inverter ACs slow the compressor down instead of switching it on and off, so they usually handle long hot days more smoothly and use less power. But they depend on sensors and an electronic board, and in very high heat or voltage swings they may reduce output to protect themselves. Non-inverter ACs run the compressor at full speed and are more sensitive to low voltage and a weak capacitor. Either way, a clean outdoor unit is the single biggest factor in summer performance.

How to keep your AC cooling all summer

  • Get a full AC service in February–March, before the heat; see the best time to service your AC in Andhra Pradesh.
  • Wash filters every two weeks from April to June.
  • Shade the outdoor unit from direct afternoon sun without blocking its airflow.
  • Use 24–26°C with a ceiling fan instead of 18°C.

post.ac-gas-filling-cost-r32-vs-r410a.bo:
Quick answer: in 2026, AC gas filling for a typical home split AC in India usually costs about ₹2,000–₹3,500, and can reach ₹4,500 in some cities or for larger units. In Narasaraopet, BOBBY's estimate range is ₹2,000–₹3,500 per AC, including a leak check. R32 is now the most common gas in new Indian ACs; R410A is found in many older and some commercial units. The bigger cost question is not the gas type but whether a leak is repaired first.

R32 vs R410A: what is the difference?

R32R410AR22 (old)
Global warming potential (GWP)675about 2,088about 1,810
Ozone depletionZeroZeroDepletes ozone (being phased out)
CompositionSingle gasBlend of two gasesSingle gas
Top-upCan be topped up on siteUsually recover and recharge fullyOld units only
Where you find itMost new inverter split ACsOlder split and some commercial ACsOlder window/split ACs

R32 has roughly one-third the global warming impact of R410A, which is why most manufacturers have moved to it. Because R32 is a single-component gas, it can be topped up without changing its composition; R410A is a blend, so a careful technician usually recovers it and recharges by weight. Both R32 and R410A run at high pressure, so the right gauges and tools matter.

Never mix gases

Your AC is designed for one refrigerant; it is printed on the outdoor unit's rating sticker. Filling R32 into an R410A system (or the reverse) damages performance and can harm the compressor. A genuine technician always reads the sticker first.

What affects the price

  • How much gas is needed: a small top-up costs less than a full recharge after a big leak.
  • Leak repair: finding and brazing or re-flaring the leak adds cost but saves you a repeat refill.
  • Vacuuming: after a leak or repair, the system should be vacuumed to remove air and moisture before charging.
  • Pipe length and tonnage: bigger ACs and long pipe runs hold more refrigerant.
  • Inverter vs non-inverter: not usually a big price difference for gas itself.

Signs your AC really needs gas

  • Cooling has dropped gradually over weeks, not suddenly.
  • Ice or frost on the thinner copper pipe or the indoor coil.
  • The outdoor unit runs, but the large pipe is not cold to touch.
  • Oily marks at pipe joints or valves (refrigerant carries oil).
  • A hissing sound near the joints.

If cooling stopped suddenly, or the outdoor fan is not running, the problem is more likely electrical (capacitor, contactor, PCB) than gas.

Gas filling in inverter ACs

Most inverter ACs in India use R32. The process is the same (leak check, repair, vacuum, charge by weight to the nameplate figure), but inverter systems are sensitive to overcharging, so "adding a little extra" is a mistake. A correct charge matters for efficiency and compressor life.

How to avoid overpaying

  • Ask for the pressure reading before and after.
  • Ask where the leak was and how it was fixed.
  • Confirm the gas type matches the outdoor unit sticker.
  • Get the price confirmed before the work starts.

The honest way to fill AC gas

  1. Check cooling, airflow and filters: many "gas problems" are actually dirty coils.
  2. Measure the pressure against the gas type on the sticker.
  3. If low, find the leak (joints, valves, coils) and repair it.
  4. Vacuum the system.
  5. Charge the correct gas to the manufacturer's standard.
  6. Test cooling and pressures before leaving.

post.refrigerator-not-cooling-causes-sol: Refrigerator Not Cooling – Common Causes and Solutions
A warm fridge puts food at risk. Learn the right temperature, the 8 most common causes, what you can fix safely at home and when you need a technician.

Quick answer: a refrigerator should stay at or below 4°C, with the freezer at about −18°C. If it is not cooling, check the temperature setting, the door gasket, the space behind the fridge and the condenser coils first. If the compressor is silent, it clicks repeatedly, or the freezer is cold but the fridge section is warm, it usually needs a technician.

What temperature should a fridge be?

Food-safety agencies such as the US FDA recommend keeping the refrigerator at or below 4°C (40°F) and the freezer at −18°C (0°F). Above 4°C, bacteria grow faster and food spoils sooner. Most fridge dials do not show actual temperatures, so an inexpensive fridge thermometer is the easiest way to check.

8 common reasons a refrigerator stops cooling

CauseSignsCan you fix it?
Wrong thermostat settingEverything slightly warmYes: set to the middle/recommended level
Door not sealingFrost near the door, gasket dirty or looseClean it; replace if torn
No space behind fridgeHot sides, compressor runs longYes: leave gap at back and sides
Dusty condenser coilsWeak cooling, high billsGentle cleaning (unplugged)
Overloaded / blocked ventsCold in some places, warm in othersYes: rearrange food
Defrost problem (frost-free)Freezer iced up, fridge warmTechnician
Fan or sensor faultNo airflow inside, uneven coolingTechnician
Compressor / relay / gas leakCompressor silent or clicking, no coolingTechnician

Safe checks you can do at home

  1. Check power and setting: make sure it is plugged in properly and the thermostat is not on the lowest level.
  2. Paper test on the door seal: close the door on a sheet of paper. If it slides out easily, the gasket is not sealing. Clean it with warm water and mild soap.
  3. Give it space: manufacturers recommend a gap of about 5–10 cm at the back and sides so heat can escape.
  4. Clean the coils: unplug the fridge and gently brush dust from the condenser coils at the back or bottom.
  5. Do not overpack: leave room around the air vents inside.
  6. Wait 24 hours after cleaning or moving the fridge for temperatures to settle.

Warning signs that need a technician

  • The compressor is silent, or clicks on and off every few minutes.
  • The freezer is cold but the fridge section is warm (often a defrost or fan fault in frost-free models).
  • Heavy ice keeps building up on the back wall.
  • Water collects under or inside the fridge.
  • A burning smell or the fridge trips the MCB.

BOBBY repairs single door and double door refrigerators at your home in Narasaraopet: inspection first, estimate before work. The visit charge is typically ₹300–₹500 plus parts if needed; see a quick estimate or book refrigerator repair.

Direct cool vs frost-free: different problems

Direct cool (usually single door) fridges cool by natural convection and need manual defrosting. Thick ice on the freezer plate blocks cooling, so defrost when ice is more than about half a centimetre thick. Frost-free fridges use a fan and an automatic defrost heater; when the defrost system or fan fails, the freezer may stay cold while the lower fridge section warms up.

Power cuts and voltage

Frequent power cuts and low voltage are hard on fridge compressors. After a power cut, give the fridge a few minutes before switching on repeatedly, and use a suitable stabiliser if your area sees big voltage swings. Keep the door closed during outages: a full freezer stays cold much longer than a half-empty one.

Repair or replace?

Most cooling problems (thermostat, relay, fan, door seal, defrost parts) are worth repairing. A compressor or major gas-leak repair on a very old fridge is where it makes sense to compare the repair cost with a new, more efficient model. Look at the BEE star label on a new fridge to compare annual power use.

Tips to keep a fridge cooling well

  • Let hot food cool before putting it in.
  • Clean the door gasket monthly.
  • Do not keep the fridge next to a stove or in direct sun.
  • Use a stabiliser if your area has frequent voltage swings.
  • Read our refrigerator maintenance guide.
post.washing-machine-not-spinning-causes: Washing Machine Not Spinning – Causes and Repair Options
Clothes still soaking wet? Find out why washing machines stop spinning, what to check safely, and when the belt, motor or control board needs repair.

Quick answer: most washing machines that stop spinning have an unbalanced load, water that has not drained (blocked filter or hose), or a door/lid lock that is not engaging. Machines will not spin until water drains and the load is balanced. If the drum still does not turn with a small, even load, the drive belt, motor, motor capacitor or control board may need repair.

Why the spin cycle stops

Modern washing machines protect themselves. Sensors check the load balance, water level and door lock before high-speed spin. If any check fails, the machine slows down, keeps trying to rebalance, or stops with an error code. That is why the first checks are simple ones.

Common causes, from simple to serious

1. Unbalanced load

One heavy item (a blanket or jeans) or a tangled bedsheet throws the drum off-balance. Samsung, for example, shows codes such as "Ub" or "Ur" for this. Redistribute the clothes or add similar items, then run Spin only.

2. Water not draining

A machine will not spin while water remains. Check for a kinked or blocked drain hose, and on front loaders clean the debris (pump) filter near the bottom front. Coins, hair clips and lint often block it.

3. Machine not level

An uneven floor makes the machine vibrate and the sensors cut the spin. Adjust the legs until it sits firm and level.

4. Lid or door lock problem

If the lock does not engage, the machine will not spin for safety. A worn lock or a faulty switch needs replacement.

5. Worn or broken drive belt

Common in older top loaders and semi-automatics: the motor runs (you hear it) but the drum barely turns.

6. Motor, capacitor or coupling fault

A humming sound with no movement can point to a weak motor capacitor or a motor/coupling issue.

7. Control board or sensor fault

Repeated error codes after the basics are checked usually point to a sensor or the PCB.

Quick checks before you call

Always unplug the machine before opening the filter, and never try to open the back panel yourself.

How to prevent spin problems

  • Do not overload, and do not wash a single heavy item alone.
  • Clean the front loader debris filter every month or two.
  • Empty pockets: coins and hairpins are the top cause of drain pump damage.
  • Use the right amount of detergent; too much foam can stop the spin.
  • Keep the machine level and on a firm floor.

post.best-time-to-service-ac-in-andhra-p: Best Time to Service Your AC in Andhra Pradesh (Month-by-Month Guide)
Beat the April rush: a simple AC service calendar for Andhra Pradesh's climate, from the pre-summer service to the post-monsoon check.

Quick answer: in Andhra Pradesh the best time to service your AC is February to mid-March, before the summer heat and the April–May rush. Plan a second check after the monsoon (October–November) if your AC runs a lot, and wash the filters every two weeks during peak summer.

Why timing matters in Andhra Pradesh

Coastal Andhra and Palnadu district get long, hot summers. IMD heatwave alerts in April and May regularly report 44–46°C in many districts. That is when every AC in town is running flat out, and when technicians are busiest. A dirty or slightly faulty AC that limps through March often fails in the first heatwave. Servicing it a few weeks earlier means better cooling, lower bills and no waiting for a technician in 45°C heat.

What a proper pre-summer service includes

  • Filter washing and indoor coil cleaning.
  • Outdoor condenser coil and fin cleaning (see outdoor unit cleaning).
  • Drain line flushing to prevent leaks.
  • Electrical connections and capacitor check.
  • Refrigerant pressure and cooling performance check.

If your AC smells musty or airflow is weak, choose AC deep cleaning instead of a basic service.

How often should you service an AC?

For most homes in Andhra Pradesh: one full service before summer, and a second after the monsoon if the AC runs many hours a day, is near a dusty road, or is in a shop or clinic. Filters should be cleaned far more often: every two weeks in peak summer.

Signs you should not wait for the "right" month

  • Water dripping from the indoor unit.
  • Burning smell, sparks or the MCB tripping (switch off immediately).
  • Ice on pipes or sudden loss of cooling.
  • Loud rattling or grinding from either unit.

These need a repair visit straight away, whatever the season.

What you can do between services

  • Wash the filters (switch off first, dry fully before refitting).
  • Keep 1–2 feet of open space in front of the outdoor unit.
  • Wipe the indoor unit body and vanes with a dry cloth.
  • Use 24–26°C with a ceiling fan; it is gentler on the AC and your bill.

Shops, clinics and offices

ACs that run 10–14 hours a day in commercial spaces collect dust much faster. For these, a service every three to four months, plus monthly filter cleaning, keeps cooling and power use under control.

post.ac-installation-checklist-indian-ho: AC Installation Checklist for Indian Homes (15 Points to Check)
Bad installation causes most AC leaks, noise and weak cooling. Use this 15-point checklist before, during and after your split AC is installed.

Quick answer: a good split AC installation needs the right location for both units, a dedicated power point with proper earthing, correctly sized and sealed copper pipes, a drain pipe with a continuous downward slope, a firm outdoor stand with space to breathe, a vacuum test before start-up, and a full cooling test before the technician leaves.

Most "AC problems" we are called for in the first year (water dripping indoors, noisy outdoor units, weak cooling, gas leaks) trace back to the installation. Use this checklist whether you buy online, from a showroom or shift an old AC.

Before installation: plan the location

  1. Indoor unit height and position: about 7–8 feet high, on a strong wall, where air reaches the whole room, away from direct heat sources.
  2. Outdoor unit location: shaded if possible, with open space in front and at the sides so hot air can escape; not facing a wall closely.
  3. Distance between units: as short as practical. Very long pipe runs reduce efficiency and may need extra gas.
  4. Power point: a dedicated socket and wiring suitable for the AC load, with proper earthing and an MCB.
  5. Stabiliser: check whether your model needs one; many inverter ACs have a wide voltage range, older non-inverter ACs often need one.

During installation: what to watch

  1. Wall bracket level: the indoor unit must be level (or tilted slightly to the drain side as the manual says).
  2. Copper pipes: correct size for your model, insulated, with clean flare joints tightened properly.
  3. Drain pipe slope: a continuous downward slope with no loops, so water never flows back.
  4. Wiring: neat, secured connections; no loose joints or tape-only connections.
  5. Outdoor stand: firm wall bracket or level base with anti-vibration pads.
  6. Wall hole sealing: sealed after piping to keep out water, insects and hot air.
  7. Vacuuming: the pipes and indoor coil should be vacuumed before releasing refrigerant, to remove air and moisture.

After installation: handover checks

  1. Leak check at all joints.
  2. Cooling test: cold air within minutes, outdoor fan and compressor running smoothly, no unusual noise.
  3. Drain test: pour a little water in the indoor tray or watch condensate after 20–30 minutes; it should drain outside, not drip indoors.

A genuine installer tells you about any extras and their cost before starting. Indicative prices for pipes, brackets and drain pipe are on our AC spare parts price list.

Window AC installation tips

  • Fit it slightly tilted outward (as per the manual) so water drains outside.
  • Seal gaps around the frame to keep out hot air, dust and rain.
  • Leave the rear and sides open outside the wall so the condenser can breathe.
  • Use a strong frame or stand; never rest the weight on loose bricks.

Shifting an AC to a new house

When moving, the gas should be pumped down into the outdoor unit before uninstalling, the pipes capped, and the system vacuumed and leak-tested again at the new home. Rough uninstallation is a common cause of gas loss.

post.how-to-identify-genuine-ac-repair-t: How to Identify a Genuine AC Repair Technician (and Avoid Scams)
Fake "authorised" callers, unnecessary gas refills and swapped parts are common. Here are the checks and red flags every customer should know.

Quick answer: a genuine AC technician has a verifiable business (real phone number, address and reviews), inspects before quoting, explains the fault, gives you a clear estimate before work, shows you old parts, and gives a bill. Be careful with anyone who demands advance payment, says your AC "needs gas every year", refuses to show old parts, or claims to be "authorised" without proof.

post.ac-repair-in-narasaraopet.title: AC Repair in Narasaraopet: Common AC Problems, Repair Solutions & Doorstep Service
post.ac-repair-in-narasaraopet.excerpt: The AC problems we see most in Narasaraopet homes, what usually causes them, what a proper repair involves, and how to get a technician at your doorstep.
post.ac-repair-in-narasaraopet.body:
Quick answer: most AC breakdowns in Narasaraopet come down to six problems: weak cooling, water leakage, unusual noise, the AC not switching on, frequent tripping, and refrigerant (gas) leaks. Many start small and get expensive when ignored. A good technician inspects first, explains the fault, gives you an estimate, and only then repairs.

Narasaraopet summers regularly push past 40°C, and ACs here run long hours in dusty conditions. That is harder on an air conditioner than the "average" use manufacturers design for, which is why the same handful of faults keep coming up. This guide walks through each one, what normally causes it, what you can safely check yourself, and what a proper repair looks like.

1. AC running but not cooling

This is the most common complaint we get. Usual causes, from simplest to most serious:

  • Clogged filters blocking airflow (the cheapest fix of all).
  • Wrong mode or setting: Fan or Dry mode instead of Cool, or a timer/eco mode limiting output.
  • Dirty indoor coil or outdoor condenser: the AC cannot move heat out of the room.
  • Low refrigerant caused by a leak: weak cooling, sometimes ice on the copper pipes.
  • Electrical faults: a weak capacitor, failed sensor, or PCB problem stopping the compressor.

Our detailed guide Why is my AC not cooling properly? covers the safe checks you can do before calling anyone.

2. Water leaking from the indoor unit

Water dripping inside the room almost always means the condensate cannot drain away: a blocked drain pipe, a dirty drain tray, a kinked or badly sloped pipe, or an indoor unit that is not mounted level. Leaving it is risky because water can reach wiring and damage walls. Read more in Why is your AC leaking water?

3. Unusual noise or vibration

  • Rattling: loose panels, mounting bolts or debris in the outdoor fan.
  • Squealing or grinding: worn fan-motor bearings.
  • Clicking that repeats: relay or electrical issues.
  • Hissing or bubbling: possible refrigerant leak.

Noise is worth checking early: a worn motor caught in time is a small repair; a seized one can take other parts with it.

4. AC not switching on

Check the obvious first: remote batteries, the wall switch, the MCB, and whether the stabiliser (if you have one) is showing a fault. If power is reaching the unit but nothing happens, the cause is usually a blown fuse, a failed PCB, a faulty sensor or a wiring fault. Please do not open the electrical panel yourself.

5. AC tripping the MCB or switching off by itself

Repeated tripping points to an electrical problem: a shorted compressor or fan motor, a damaged capacitor, loose terminals, or wiring that is too thin for the AC's load. A unit that cuts out after a few minutes may also be overheating because the outdoor unit is dirty or boxed in with no airflow.

6. Refrigerant (gas) leak

Refrigerant does not get "used up". If the gas is low, there is a leak somewhere, usually at flare joints, brazed joints, or a corroded coil. Topping up without finding the leak means paying again a few weeks later. A proper job is: find the leak, repair it, pressure-test, vacuum the system, then charge the correct amount. See AC gas filling: when is it actually required?

Repair or replace? A quick guide

SituationUsually worth it
Filters, drain, capacitor, sensor, fan motorRepair: low-cost parts, big improvement
Gas leak at a jointRepair the leak, then refill
PCB fault on a fairly new ACRepair or replace the board
Compressor failure on a 10+ year old fixed-speed ACCompare the repair estimate with a new energy-efficient AC

What a proper AC repair visit should include

  1. Inspection first: checking the indoor and outdoor units, electrical readings and cooling performance.
  2. A clear explanation of the fault in simple language.
  3. An estimate before work starts, with your approval needed for any parts.
  4. The repair using suitable tools and parts.
  5. Testing the AC after the repair and telling you about anything else that needs attention.

post.how-to-reduce-ac-electricity-bill.t: How to Reduce Your AC Electricity Bill in India: 12 Practical Power-Saving Tips
post.how-to-reduce-ac-electricity-bill.e: Simple, proven ways to cut AC power use in Indian homes, from the BEE-recommended 24°C setting to filter cleaning and choosing the right tonnage.
post.how-to-reduce-ac-electricity-bill.b:
Quick answer: the single biggest saving is the temperature setting. India's Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) estimates that raising the AC setting by 1°C saves about 6% electricity, and moving from 20°C to 24°C saves about 24%. After that, clean filters, a well-ventilated outdoor unit, inverter operation and regular servicing make the biggest difference.

In most Indian homes the air conditioner is the largest single electricity load in summer. The good news is that you do not need to suffer the heat to cut the bill. These 12 tips are ordered roughly by how much they save for how little effort.

1. Set the temperature to 24°C (or higher)

BEE recommends 24°C as the default setting, and since 2020 star-labelled room ACs sold in India ship with a 24°C default. Each degree lower adds roughly 6% to consumption. Setting 18°C does not cool the room faster; it only keeps the compressor running longer.

2. Use the fan with the AC

A ceiling fan on low speed spreads cool air and makes 25–26°C feel like 23–24°C, so you can keep the thermostat higher.

3. Clean the filters every 2–3 weeks in summer

Dusty filters reduce airflow, make the compressor run longer and cut cooling. Slide them out, rinse with plain water, dry fully and refit. It takes five minutes and costs nothing.

4. Keep the outdoor unit shaded and breathing

The outdoor unit throws heat out. Direct afternoon sun, dust on the condenser fins, or walls and grills boxing it in force it to work harder. Keep at least a foot of open space around it and keep plants, boxes and clothes away from it.

5. Service the AC before summer

A full service (coil cleaning, drain check, outdoor unit cleaning, electrical checks) restores cooling efficiency that slowly drops with dust build-up. See when to service your AC.

6. Seal the room

Close doors and windows, use curtains or blinds on sun-facing windows, and block gaps under doors. Every bit of hot air that leaks in must be cooled again.

7. Use sleep mode and timers

Sleep mode gradually raises the set temperature at night as your body cools. A timer that switches the AC off in the early morning, when it is cooler outside, can save several hours of running a night.

8. Let an inverter AC run steadily

Inverter ACs save power by slowing the compressor down once the room is cool. Switching them on and off repeatedly wastes that advantage. Set a sensible temperature and let it run.

9. Choose the right tonnage

Room size (approx.)Typical AC size
Up to 120 sq ft0.8–1 ton
120–180 sq ft1–1.5 ton
180–250 sq ft1.5–2 ton

Top-floor rooms, west-facing walls, large windows and kitchens need more capacity. An undersized AC runs flat out all day; an oversized one cycles inefficiently and does not remove humidity well.

10. Read the BEE star label properly

BEE tightened its star rating thresholds from 1 January 2026, so a model rated 5-star under the 2025 table is rated 4-star under the new one. Compare the ISEER value printed on the label (higher is better) and check the label's validity period, not just the star count.

11. Avoid heat sources in the AC room

Ovens, irons, old incandescent bulbs and lots of electronics all add heat. Switch them off or use them elsewhere while the AC is running.

12. Fix gas leaks and electrical faults promptly

An AC with low refrigerant or a weak capacitor runs much longer for the same cooling. If cooling drops or the bill jumps without a reason, book a check rather than lowering the temperature further.

How much can you actually save?

As a rough example using BEE's figure: if your AC uses 300 units a month at 20°C, running it at 24°C could save around 70 units a month. Try the AC electricity cost calculator on our FAQs page to estimate your own running cost.

post.ac-technician-near-me.body:
Quick answer: a reliable AC technician near you inspects before recommending anything, explains the fault in plain language, gives an estimate before starting, uses proper tools (gauges, vacuum pump, leak detection), and tests the AC before leaving. Be wary of anyone who suggests "gas filling" without checking for a leak, or who will not tell you the charges upfront.

When your AC stops cooling in the middle of summer, it is tempting to call the first number you find. A few minutes of checking can save you a repeat visit, an unnecessary part, or a gas refill that leaks out again in a week.

Questions to ask before you book

  1. Do you work on my brand and type? (split, window, inverter)
  2. Is there a visit or inspection charge? Get it clear before the visit.
  3. When can you come? A realistic time slot is better than a vague "today".
  4. Will you give an estimate before doing any repair? The answer should be yes.
  5. Do you carry common parts? Capacitors, sensors and fuses are often fixed in one visit.

What a proper diagnosis looks like

  • Checking supply voltage and the stabiliser
  • Inspecting filters, coils and the drain
  • Measuring temperatures at the indoor unit and the copper pipes
  • Checking the outdoor unit: compressor, fan motor, capacitor
  • Using pressure gauges if a refrigerant problem is suspected

Red flags to watch for

  • "You need gas" without a leak check. Refrigerant does not get used up; low gas means a leak.
  • No price until the work is done. You should approve the estimate first.
  • Replacing the PCB or compressor straight away without testing the cheaper parts (capacitor, sensor, wiring) first.
  • No vacuum pump for installation or gas work: moisture left in the system damages the compressor.
  • Leaving without testing the cooling.

Authorised service centre or independent technician?

If your AC is under warranty, use the brand's authorised service so the warranty stays valid. After the warranty, a good independent multi-brand technician is often faster and more flexible, especially in smaller towns. post.why-is-my-ac-not-cooling.title: Why Is My AC Not Cooling Properly?
post.why-is-my-ac-not-cooling.excerpt: The most common reasons an AC runs but does not cool, and what you can safely check yourself.
post.why-is-my-ac-not-cooling.body:
An AC that runs but does not cool is the most common complaint we hear in Narasaraopet summers. The good news: the cause is often simple. Here are the usual reasons, from easiest to most serious.

1. Dirty air filters

Dust-clogged filters block airflow, so the room never gets cold. Filters in a split AC can be slid out and rinsed with plain water every two to three weeks in heavy use. Let them dry fully before refitting.

2. Wrong settings

Check the remote is on Cool mode (not Fan or Dry) and the temperature is set around 24°C. A very low setting does not cool faster; it only makes the compressor work longer.

3. Dirty or blocked outdoor unit

The outdoor unit releases heat. If it sits in direct afternoon sun, is covered with dust, or is boxed in by walls, cooling drops sharply. Keep the area around it clear.

4. Low refrigerant (gas)

If the gas has leaked, cooling becomes weak and you may see ice on the copper pipes. Gas does not get "used up", so low gas always means a leak that must be found and repaired before refilling.

5. Electrical or component faults

A weak capacitor, a faulty sensor or a PCB problem can stop the compressor from running properly. These need a technician with the right tools.

When to call a technician

If cleaning the filters and checking the settings does not help, book an inspection. Please do not open the electrical panel yourself.
post.when-should-you-service-your-ac.tit: When Should You Service Your Air Conditioner?
post.when-should-you-service-your-ac.exc: A simple servicing schedule for hot, dusty Andhra summers, and the signs your AC is overdue.
post.when-should-you-service-your-ac.bod:
Regular servicing keeps an AC cooling well, reduces power use and catches small faults before they become expensive. In a hot, dusty town like Narasaraopet, ACs work harder than the manufacturer's average, so timing matters.

A practical schedule

  • Before summer (February–March): a full service so the AC is ready for peak heat.
  • After heavy summer use (around July–August): a second service if the AC runs most of the day.
  • Filters: rinse every two to three weeks during heavy use.

Signs your AC needs servicing now

  • It takes much longer to cool the room
  • A musty or bad smell when it starts
  • Water dripping from the indoor unit
  • Unusual rattling or humming sounds
  • Your electricity bill has gone up without a reason

What a proper service includes

Cleaning the filters and indoor unit, clearing the drain line, checking the outdoor unit and fan, and checking that the AC is cooling as it should. If the technician finds a deeper problem, they should explain it and give you an estimate before doing any extra work.
AC Gas Filling: When Is It Actually Required?
Gas is not a routine top-up. Learn the real signs of low gas and why a leak check must come first.

"Your AC needs gas" is one of the most common things people hear when their AC is not cooling. Sometimes it is true. Often, it is not. Here is how to tell the difference.

AC gas does not run out on its own

The refrigerant in your AC moves in a sealed loop. It is not burned or used up like petrol. If the gas level is low, there is a leak somewhere: at a joint, a valve or a damaged pipe.

Signs that may point to low gas

  • Cooling has slowly become weaker over weeks
  • Ice or frost on the copper pipes or indoor coil
  • A hissing or bubbling sound near the pipes
  • The outdoor unit runs but the air inside is only slightly cool

Problems that look the same but are not gas

Dirty filters, a clogged indoor coil, a dusty outdoor unit, a weak capacitor or a faulty fan motor can all cause poor cooling. Filling gas will not fix any of these.

The right order of work

  1. Inspect the AC and measure the pressure
  2. Find and repair the leak if there is one
  3. Fill gas to the correct level for your model
  4. Test the cooling performance

Ask your technician to explain which of these steps your AC needs before you agree to gas filling.
post.why-is-your-ac-leaking-water.title: Why Is Your AC Leaking Water?
post.why-is-your-ac-leaking-water.excerp: Water dripping from the indoor unit is common and usually fixable. Here are the causes.
post.why-is-your-ac-leaking-water.body:
An AC removes moisture from the room air. That water is meant to flow out through a drain pipe, usually outside the wall. When it drips from the indoor unit instead, one of these is usually the reason.

Blocked drain pipe

Dust and algae can block the drain line, especially if the AC has not been serviced for a while. The water backs up and overflows from the indoor unit. This is the most common cause and is cleared during servicing.

Dirty filters causing ice

Clogged filters reduce airflow, the coil gets too cold and forms ice. When the ice melts, more water than the tray can handle drips into the room.

Incorrect installation slope

The indoor unit must tilt slightly towards the drain side. If it was mounted perfectly level or tilted the wrong way, water collects and leaks.

Damaged drain tray or pipe

A cracked tray or a disconnected or kinked pipe will leak even when everything else is fine.

What to do

Switch the AC off if water is reaching electrical points or furniture, wipe the area dry, and book a service. Most leaks are fixed by cleaning the drain line and filters or correcting the unit's slope.
post.split-ac-vs-window-ac.title: Split AC vs Window AC: Which Suits Your Home?
post.split-ac-vs-window-ac.excerpt: A plain comparison of installation, noise, cooling and upkeep to help you choose.
post.split-ac-vs-window-ac.body:
Both split and window ACs cool a room well when they are the right size and properly installed. The best choice depends on your room, your walls and your budget.

Window AC

  • One single unit fitted in a window or a wall opening
  • Usually lower purchase and installation cost
  • Simpler to remove and shift
  • Louder, because the compressor sits in the same unit
  • Needs a suitable window or opening

Split AC

  • Indoor unit on the wall, outdoor unit outside, joined by copper pipes
  • Much quieter inside the room
  • More placement options and a cleaner look
  • Installation needs piping, drilling and correct gas handling
  • Generally better suited to larger rooms

Quick guide

Choose a window AC for a small room with a suitable window, rented homes, or a tight budget. Choose a split AC when you want quiet cooling, a larger room, or the room has no suitable window.

Installation matters for both

Correct mounting, sealing, drain slope and electrical connection decide how well and how long your AC works. Whichever type you choose, get it installed and tested properly.
post.how-to-maintain-your-refrigerator.e: Easy habits that keep your fridge cooling well, plus the warning signs that need a technician.
post.how-to-maintain-your-refrigerator.b:
A refrigerator runs 24 hours a day, every day. A few simple habits keep it cooling well, save electricity and help it last longer.

Give it space to breathe

Leave a gap of a few inches between the back of the fridge and the wall so heat can escape. Keep it away from the stove and direct sunlight.

Keep the door seal clean

Wipe the rubber gasket with a damp cloth. If the door does not close firmly or the seal is torn, cold air leaks out and the compressor works harder.

Do not overload it

Cold air needs to circulate. Packing shelves tightly or blocking the vents inside causes uneven cooling. Let hot food cool down before putting it in.

Clean the back and the drain

Dust on the condenser at the back reduces cooling. Unplug the fridge before gently cleaning it. In frost-free models, a blocked drain hole causes water to collect at the bottom.

Signs you need a technician

  • The fridge runs but does not cool, or the freezer cools but the fridge does not
  • Water collecting inside or under the fridge
  • Loud clicking, buzzing or the compressor running non-stop
  • Heavy ice build-up in a frost-free model
